result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: add_members does `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` then `group.add(user)` — no else branch, no error/success detail — and the client-side `addMembers` in group.js just calls `self.findMembers()` on success, so a typo'd username is silently ignored with no feedback. This is real, specific, and grounded in new code, but it mirrors the pre-existing behavior of the old update_patch (which also silently skipped unknown usernames), so it is a substantive UX/feedback concern rather than a newly introduced correctness defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are processed with `usernames.split(",").each` and only added if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; non-existent usernames are simply skipped (`if user = ... group.add(user) end`) and the action still renders `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. On the client side, `Group#addMembers` just reloads the member list via `self.findMembers()` with no way to surface partial failures. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/feedback gap, but not a verifiable correctness defect (the server intentionally treats unknown users as no-ops).
